title: A birthday for our Lilo & Stitch fan.
summary: A Lilo & Stitch birthday at the Children’s Museum of Greater Fall River: homemade decorations, family photographs, and a museum rental memory with party-planning links.
search: Fall River, Massachusetts · A birthday memoryA birthday for our Lilo & Stitch fan.We rented out the Children’s Museum of Greater Fall River for James’s birthday, made the decorations ourselves, and brought a little of his favorite world along.From our February 2019 family album · Published October 22, 2026The party table, ready for everyone. Oh, this birthday. Looking back at these photographs makes me so grateful all over again. James’s great love of Lilo & Stitch made the theme an easy decision. We rented out the Children’s Museum of Greater Fall River and gathered everyone together to celebrate him. At the time, Lilo & Stitch wasn’t nearly as popular a party theme, so I made the decorations myself. Pineapple cups, flowers, tropical leaves, and Stitch himself at the table. A little February escape, right in Fall River. A little tropical color for a February birthday.Stitch had a place at the party, of course. There was the party, and there was a whole museum to explore. I love having both kinds of photographs: the table before everyone arrived, when you could still see all the work that went into it, and the room with everyone gathered around it. The people who made the day special. What stays with me most is everyone who helped make it special. When you’re planning a celebration for your child, you hope they’ll feel happy, welcomed, and surrounded by people who love them. We’re still so grateful to everyone who showed up for James and celebrated with us—and, of course, to the museum staff for helping make it such a lovely day. Time to explore the museum, too.Another little moment from the family album. A birthday built around something he loved, with people who love him. That’s a memory I’ll always treasure. Thinking about a museum birthday?Start with what your child enjoys, then ask the venue about the details that would help your family: private use, a place to take a break, entrances and exits, and time to set up. Our party is a family memory from 2019; confirm today’s arrangements directly.The museum is at 441 North Main Street, Fall River, Massachusetts. search: Home / Journal / Little Things That Help The family notebook · Little Things That Help · No. 01 Sometimes the straw is the whole trick. INTENSE strawberry milk from Wegmans, a preferred straw, and two free picture cards for everyday choices. We brought home a bottle of INTENSE® Lowfat Strawberry Milk from Wegmans. At the kitchen counter, a bendy straw gave us something else to think about: the way someone wants to drink it matters, too. See what we tried ↓ From our kitchen: the bottle, the red cap, and the bendy straw. A small domestic discoveryKeep the familiar thing. Change the fiddly part. We wanted to keep the straw where it belonged while using the bottle. Our first try used a small opening in the red cap to hold it in place. We took photographs because it was the sort of little household adjustment we wanted to remember. What stayed with us was the question behind it: if someone already knows the drink they want, can we make the next step simpler? How a bottle is held, where a straw sits, and how a preference is expressed all belong in an everyday product conversation. The bottle and its cap, before the straw. The cap detail from our first test. A practical noteFor the next drink.The photographed cap was a one-off experiment, not a product recommendation or a leakproof setup. For repeat use, choose a compatible, food-safe straw lid or a reusable lidded cup; hand-cut plastic can leave sharp edges or loose pieces. Keep reusable parts clean and follow the milk’s refrigeration directions. For the communication toolkit A picture for the preference. We made two printable prompts to go with this note: STRAWBERRY MILK and STRAW. Use them separately for the drink and the way to drink it, or make a card with a photograph of your own bottle.
